causal_chain: A candidate-conditioned history router can select a sparse support subset and a sparse suppression subset from the user's interacted items instead of collapsing history into one static user vector.
Because full-sort ranking evaluates many near-neighbor items, item-specific retrieval over history should especially help hard comparisons where static collaborative embeddings blur multiple intents.

If this routed evidence is genuinely useful rather than just extra capacity, gains should concentrate on users with longer or more diverse histories and on candidates whose top supporting history items are few and high-confidence.

The support path raises scores when a candidate aligns with a coherent local taste pattern, while the suppression path lowers scores when the candidate mainly matches historically conflicting or popularity-driven evidence.
Users with mixed or noisy histories contain both supportive and misleading past interactions for any given candidate item.
blind_projection.closest_parent: A recommender that learns which historical interactions most support each positive target and explicitly trains ranking margins to remain stable when those support interactions are removed will generalize better in offline top-n recommendation than a matched model trained only on factual pairwise ranking, because it suppresses brittle shortcut co-occurrence reliance and promotes support-distributed user representations.
blind_projection.competing_explanation: Any measured gain could come from increased scorer flexibility or higher effective item-item capacity rather than from candidate-conditioned support/suppression routing itself.
discriminative_predictions: Ablating only the suppression path should hurt more on popularity-skewed candidates and broad-taste users, while ablating only the support sparsification should mostly hurt hard positive recovery among semantically close alternatives.

If the mechanism is real, the top routed support items for a held-out positive should be few and concentrated; a diffuse attention pattern with equal performance would favor the capacity-only explanation.

Relative to a matched control with the same embedding backbone but no candidate-conditioned routing, the proposed model should show larger improvements for users with longer and more interaction-diverse histories than for very short-history users.
expected_evidence: Inspection of routed support/suppression sparsity statistics can verify whether the model actually uses selective history retrieval instead of collapsing to near-uniform aggregation.
Qualification runs can compare full-sort NDCG@10 against a parameter-matched mechanism-off control under the frozen ML-1M protocol.
Slice analysis by user history length, history entropy, and item popularity can test whether gains appear where candidate-conditioned evidence routing is supposed to matter.
blind_projection.falsifier: If a matched control that preserves the same embeddings and projection dimensions but replaces candidate-conditioned support/suppression routing with uniform or static history aggregation matches or exceeds NDCG@10, and the proposed model shows no concentrated benefit on long or diverse-history users, the routing mechanism claim is falsified.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: This is a high-change proposal because it replaces static user representation scoring with candidate-conditioned set retrieval over each user's interacted-item history, adds an explicit dual evidence decomposition into support and suppression, and requires a new full-sort scorer that computes per-candidate history routing rather than using only a precomputed user vector or standard graph propagation.
blind_projection.hypothesis: A candidate-conditioned dual-evidence history router that scores each item by combining direct user-item affinity with sparse support retrieval and sparse suppression retrieval from the user's historical items will improve full-sort NDCG@10 over static collaborative filters on ML-1M, because it can explain away misleading mixed-taste evidence while amplifying the small subset of interactions most relevant to each candidate.
implementation_requirements: Implement a candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender that stores train-only user interaction histories as padded item-id lists and masks.

Include a mechanism-off variant that preserves embeddings and combination layers but replaces candidate-conditioned routing with static uniform history aggregation and disables suppression subtraction.

Learn user embeddings, item embeddings, and two candidate-history compatibility functions producing support logits and suppression logits from candidate item embeddings and historical item embeddings.
Provide efficient full-sort scoring by batching candidate items against each user's padded history with masking, without reading held-out interactions.

Use sparse normalized routing weights over history for both channels, aggregate support and suppression history representations, and combine them with direct affinity through a small gating module to produce pairwise scores.
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Use the same item/user embedding sizes, same projection widths, same pairwise loss, same optimizer family, and the same train-only history tensors; only remove candidate-conditioned support/suppression routing in the control so the isolatable wedge is the routed dual-evidence mechanism itself.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Introduce a dual-channel candidate-conditioned evidence router over user history: for candidate item j and user u, compute support weights and suppression weights over the items in u's train history, aggregate separate support and suppression history summaries, and score j using direct affinity plus gated support minus gated suppression.
blind_projection.mechanism_off_definition: Mechanism-off is a matched static-history scorer: keep identical embeddings, projections, and final scoring head, but replace candidate-conditioned support and suppression weights with a single uniform or learned global history aggregation independent of the candidate item, and remove the subtractive suppression term. This yields a history-aware but non-routed control.
blind_projection.minimal_testable_wedge: Add only the candidate-conditioned dual support/suppression routing module on top of a shared embedding backbone, versus a matched static-history aggregation control under the same pairwise training loop.
blind_projection.research_question: Does candidate-conditioned routing over a user's historical items, with explicit support and suppression channels, improve frozen-protocol full-sort NDCG@10 beyond what can be achieved by a matched static-history collaborative scorer on ML-1M?
blind_projection.resource_hypothesis: A compact implementation with padded histories, embedding dimension in the baseline regime, and batched full-sort scoring via matrix multiplications over user-history-by-item blocks should fit the qualification budget on ML-1M, though inference batching must be carefully chunked to control memory due to candidate-conditioned routing.
